here's what you do:

Prep your jars

drill two holes in your mason jar lid. fill one hole with heat resistant silicone, this is where you will be injecting your spores into. Let the silicone cure. While you're waiting, rinse your rye grain berries until the water becomes clear. fill your mason jars with rye grain berries, but leave a couple inches at the top for shaking.

Once your lids are ready, cut a square or circle of tyvek envelope big enough to completely cover the mouth of the jar, and leave an inch on each side for leeway. the point of the tyvek is to allow the growing mycelium to breath (they need oxygen and expell CO2) while acting as a filter for micro-organisms that can contaminate your shit. prep as many jars as you want. it's likely on your first couple tries some will get contaminated.

Sterilize your jars

Once you've got your jars prepped, they need to be sterilized to kill any micro-organisms that will compete with your mycelium. Put an inch or 2 of water into your pressure cooker. Line the bottom with the spare ring screw tops that come with your mason jars. You don't want your jars touching the bottom or sides of your cooker, as it may burn the grain. Put as many jars as you can fit into the pressure cooker and cook it at 15 PSI for an hour. If you have one of those pressure cookers that doesn't let you choose, use the bean setting and run it twice. When it's done, just let it cool down overnight. The next day remove the jars. If they're still warm, set them on the counter and wait until they're room temperature. You don't want to kill your spores when you inject them.

Injecting your spores

When your jars have reached room temperature it's time to inoculate them. Take off your clothes, take a shower, wash your hands again, put on latex/vinyl gloves. Rub down your gloves with 70% isopropyl alcohol. Do not use 90% or 99%. The water content in 70% tricks bacteria into letting the alcohol through their cell membranes. Then rub down your alcohol bottle with alcohol, then rub down your gloves again. You need to be STERILE. Rub down everything you're going to touch with alcohol. You should still be naked at this point, clothing is too easy to carry around micro-organisms.

Get your spore syringe out. Shake the shit out of it. Burn the needle until it's red hot, then get rid of the soot by wiping it down with alcohol. Alternately, you can use an alcohol burner to prevent soot. I still wipe down the needle with alcohol after to cool it down. Pierce the silicone and tyvek envelope with your spore syringe and shoot some in. It doesn't take many spores to do the job, 1 could theoretically do the trick, but the more you put in the better your chance of success.

After each jar repeat burning and wiping the needle with alcohol before inoculating the next jar. After inoculation is done, shake the jar vigorously to get an even distribution of spores. If you skip this step colonization of your grain will take longer because the spores will be concentrated in one area.

Colonization

After inoculating your jars, put them in a dark area. I put mine in a closet. Make sure the temperature is around 70 degrees F. Wait a couple weeks. Depending on the strain it could take 1-5 weeks before they're ready. They need darkness during this time, don't expose them to too much light. You can check on them every couple days for contamination, but don't expose them to direct light. If you see green in your jar, throw it away without opening it. If you see red, throw it away without opening. If you see black, throw it away without opening it. If you see blue, it means they're not getting enough air. Do not open the jar. The hole without silicone and tyvek filter will provide plenty of air exchange, just make sure there's enough fresh air wherever you're putting them.

When the jars are fully white, they're almost ready, but don't rush it. Wait until the mycelium starts to pull away from the sides of the jar, that's when you'll know it's ready.

Sterilizing your straw

Get a big ass pot. fill it with water. Put the straw in. Boil that shit for an hour. The straw doesn't need to be super sterile like the jars during inoculation, but you want to kill any micro-organisms that are living in the straw. How much straw you need will depend on how many shrooms you wanna grow. There's not really a limit here. Strain your straw. Get all the loose water out of it, but don't dry it. Once it's cooled down, put it in a trash bag. Put the trash bag in a box, cardboard or plastic, I don't give a shit. I keep my straw about 8-12 inches thick. Spread it out in the box evenly. Try not to have any straws poking straight up, make the top surface flat as you can.

Poke holes in the bottom of the back, and a hole in your box to drain stagnant water.

The Grow

You can either use a lid for your box, or just leave it open. A lid is recommended for better humidity control, but it not a requirement. If you get a lid, use a plastic cover that raises up about a foot above your straw. Make holes for air in the lid. Shrooms like 99% humidity, you can get a mechanical humidity gauge, don't use a shitty digital one. When your jar is ready (mycelium contracting from the walls of your jar) shake it up. This is going to damage it and it won't start growing right away until it heals, but it's necessary. It can be hard to break it up, you may want to strip down, glove up, sterlize and break it up by hand. Break it up into golf ball sized chunks. Put it in your straw. I like to put mine in the middle of the straw, so it can grow in all directions.

You want to keep the grow area around 75 F, 99% humidity inside the box. You'll do this by spraying it several times a day. While you're spraying it, fan the straw to get rid of the CO2 and introduce fresh air. Growth time will be highly dependent on the strain, patience is required. You'll start seeing colonization soon. If you see green, you have failed. If you see blue it means it's either too dry, or not enough fresh air. Keep up spraying and fanning several times a day until you see small pins start forming. Then keep spraying and fanning several times a day.

Harvesting

Mushrooms grow from pin to ready to harvest insanely fast. You'll need to watch more closely when the pins start to form.

You'll know your mushrooms are ready to harvest when the veil begins to tear. The veil is a soft very thin membrane on the underside of the cap. When it tears, spores will rain down. Try to harvest before the veil tears. Experience will let you know when this will happen. To harvest, grasp the base of the mushroom stalk and twist. You'll probably pull up some mycelium and straw during this, that's ok. Weigh your mushrooms. They are 90% water. a 40oz mushroom when fully dry will give you 4oz. When you read about mushroom dosages they're usually talked about in dry weight. Keep track of which mushroom weighs how much, because when you're ready to consume them they may not be fully dry, and if they're not you won't know how much you're taking.

After harvesting your mushrooms, keep going. One batch of straw will get you several harvests before the mycelium can no longer produce mushrooms from the nutrients in the straw.

If done right, and depending on how much straw you used, you will net anywhere from 4oz to tens of pounds of dried mushrooms.

You can eat fresh mushrooms with the same effect as dry, just keep in mind that a 40oz fresh mushroom will get you a 4oz dry dosage.

You can use either a food dehydrator, or just put them behind your computer fan. At this point contamination is not an immediate. If you don't plan on consuming your mushrooms within a week or two, you need to dry them. When they crumble to flakes and dust when you squeeze them, they're "cracker dry".

Consuming

You can eat a whole fresh or dry mushroom if you have a strong stomach. We're unable to digest mushrooms, so it will cause nausea. I'm not a fucking pussy so I will often times just chow down on one.
